source.title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems

accepted.question_text: How can one explain and model why some social organizations thrive and enhance their core capabilities when faced with a crisis while other social organizations fail, where a social organization is a formal or informal group of interrelated individuals pursuing a collective goal and embedded in an environment? A usable answer should account for the organization's vulnerability or susceptibility to disruptions, its anticipation, foresight, or situational awareness for those vulnerabilities, and its adaptive capacity, flexibility, or fluidity in mitigating vulnerabilities or responding to disruptions.

How can one define and measure macro-variables for social organizations that quantify adaptive capacity, elasticity, robustness, and capacity to recover, so that resilience can be monitored over time and early-warning tools can be applied rather than relying only on resources, well-being surveys, or hindsight cases?

For a signed social-organization network decomposed into triads, how can structural robustness be measured so that triads are not treated as independent, relation weights are incorporated, and the importance or impact of the agents in each triad affects the collective robustness estimate?

When constructing an interaction network from time-stamped observations of a social organization using a sliding aggregation window or a time threshold Delta t, how should the window size or threshold be chosen so that network density, topological analyses, and reconstructed temporal paths for possible influence are reliable?

Given multiple reconstructed measures for agents, signed relations, interaction propensities, potentiality, robustness, adaptivity, and resilience in a social-organization model, how should those measures be combined or aggregated optimally when ground truth is often unavailable and validation must rely on in-sample and out-of-sample prediction?

In a network model of a social organization, how can interventions that change selected agents' utilities, signed relations, collaboration costs, or link structure be modeled well enough to reproduce and predict counterintuitive resilience effects such as removal of some agents stabilizing the organization?

trace.notes: Normalized the single input as a zbMATH resolver URL with trailing identifier 7825297 and source name 7825297. Local resolver metadata in outputs/shards/open-problems-shard-0.csv and outputs/open-problems-0418-all.csv identified the exact title, DOI 10.1142/S021952592250014X, and arXiv identifier 2301.00183.

Resolved the bibliographic record to the arXiv record and then to an ETH-hosted PDF linked from the authors' publication page. The resolved PDF title and authors match the zbMATH/arXiv/DOI metadata. Local shell fetching of zbmath.org, api.zbmath.org, and direct PDFs failed because outbound network access is unavailable in the sandbox, so readable full text was obtained through the page-reading tool rather than local curl.

Mapped a 54-page PDF with the section hierarchy: abstract, introduction, resilience background, defining social resilience, modeling social organizations, calculating resilience, data and control, conclusions, and references. Likely question regions were the section-opening question blocks and the explicit open/problem statements in the discussions of organizational resilience factors, missing macro-variables, structural balance, temporal interaction windows, calibration/validation, and network interventions.
